Pro Diver

Dive · 38–47mm · 200–300m · automatic · 1990–2026

The Pro Diver family is a line of dive-style watches known for its classic design cues, often drawing inspiration from iconic dive watches. It is defined by its combination of professional-grade water resistance and accessible pricing, making it a popular entry point into automatic timepieces.

The story

Introduced in the 1990s after the brand's American relaunch, the Pro Diver line gained significant popularity in the early 2000s. The family has always been characterized by its strong resemblance to the Rolex Submariner, offering a similar aesthetic with a rotating bezel, Mercedes-style hands, and a magnified date window. Early automatic models were powered by Japanese Miyota movements, later transitioning to the popular Seiko NH35A caliber. Over the years, the collection has expanded to include Swiss-made versions with ETA or Sellita movements, larger "Grand Diver" models with increased water resistance, and vintage-inspired editions like the "1953" series, solidifying its place as a cornerstone of the brand.
